evidence.note: Reads run_tests + scoring script, finds file mapping, computes method distribution across golden.jsonl — enumerating exactly which methods/files are exercised before building.

Systematically samples per-method golden responses, catalogs distinct hover shapes, studies selectionRange nesting, folding kinds, and inspects exact line content to pin down position/range boundaries.
Builds a dedicated dump.rs AST-inspection tool and dumps multiple files' ASTs to reverse-engineer the AST shape JDT-LS analyzes internally.

Launches five Agent subtasks each writing an explicit per-method spec of the expected response format (hover, folding, documentSymbol, semanticTokens, definition/references/highlight) — an explicit internal contract.
Forms and tests hypotheses about folding-order semantics against the data — distinguishing format rules from arbitrary output.
Mid-build reverse-engineering of javadoc trigger rules from multiple golden examples (name+arity, @Override correlation), re-probing when hover mismatches appear.
Continues re-inspecting golden/AST structure (spread_parameter, enhanced_for fields) whenever ref/highlight mismatches reveal a misunderstood contract detail — inquiry sustained deep into the build.

reasoning: The agent spent ~50 steps on contract discovery before writing its first source file and continued re-probing golden.jsonl and the AST every time a mismatch surfaced, sustaining this across hundreds of steps. It cataloged every method, extracted concrete exemplars, pinned down position indexing / range boundaries / folding kinds, and even wrote explicit per-method spec documents (steps 85-91) — matching the level-8 anchor fully and reaching into level 10 via multi-example invariant derivation and continuous re-probing on mismatch. I score 9 rather than 10 because the log exposes titles only, leaving the depth of JDT-LS convention cross-checking not fully verifiable.
